record.paper_title: Open Questions about Ramsey-Type Statements in Reverse Mathematics
record.original_question: Over RCA0, does the Erdős-Moser theorem imply the cohesiveness principle COH?

evidence.quote: COH is the statement “Every uniform sequence of sets R~ has an R~ -cohesive set.”
Question 4.3 Does EM imply COH over RCA0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the language of second-order arithmetic with the base theory RCA₀ (Recursive Comprehension Axiom). 

Definitions:
- A tournament on an infinite set X ⊆ ℕ is an irreflexive binary relation T on X such that for all distinct x, y ∈ X exactly one of T(x,y) or T(y,x) holds. T is transitive if T(x,y) and T(y,z) imply T(x,z).
- The Erdős–Moser theorem (EM) is the statement: every infinite tournament on ℕ has an infinite transitive subtournament.
- For a sequence R⃗ = ⟨R_n : n ∈ ℕ⟩ of subsets of ℕ, an infinite set C ⊆ ℕ is R⃗-cohesive if for every n, either C ⊆* R_n or C ⊆* ℕ ∖ R_n (where ⊆* denotes inclusion modulo a finite set).
- The cohesiveness principle (COH) is the statement: for every uniformly computable (i.e., uniformly given) sequence R⃗ of subsets of ℕ, there exists an R⃗-cohesive set.

Question: Does RCA₀ + EM prove COH?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches across recent literature on the reverse mathematics of the Erdős–Moser theorem (notably work by Patey, Lerman–Solomon–Towsner, Wang, and Monin–Patey through 2024) discuss separations involving EM (e.g., EM does not imply ADS; COH ∧ EM ∧ WKL does not imply AMT; EM has no universal instance) and construct ω-models satisfying EM together with COH, but no source found establishes either an implication EM → COH over RCA₀ or a separation. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Dominating the Erdős–Moser theorem in reverse mathematics (Patey)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs ω-models of EM ∧ WKL ∧ COH that fail AMT, but does not claim EM ⊢ COH or a separation.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes weakness results for EM but does not resolve the EM vs COH implication.

status_evidence.title: The reverse mathematics of the Thin set and Erdős–Moser theorems (Liu–Patey)
status_evidence.snippet: Proves TS and FS do not imply EM, and EM has no universal instance; no resolution of EM → COH.
status_evidence.claim: Recent paper on EM does not address the EM → COH question.

status_evidence.title: The weakness of the Erdős–Moser theorem under arithmetic reductions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies EM with respect to the arithmetic hierarchy; does not mention resolving EM vs COH.
status_evidence.claim: A 2023 paper on EM weakness does not resolve the question.
